newsitem.title: CROATIA: Forensic experts start autopsy of Ovcara victims.
newsitem.headline: Forensic experts start autopsy of Ovcara victims.

text.p: International forensic experts on Tuesday began looking into the causes of death of victims exhumed from a mass grave in eastern Croatia who investigators believe to be hospital patients executed by Serb forces in 1991.

Croatian forensic expert Davor Strinovic told state news agency HINA that the U.S.-based Physicians for Human Rights (PHR) group had started autopsies on some 200 bodies recovered from Ovcara mass grave in Serb-held eastern Slavonia.

U.N. investigators working for the Hague-based International Criminal Tribunal on former Yugoslavia, who had unearthed the bodies together with the PHR experts, began shipping them to a morgue in Zagreb for forensic examination last week.

The bodies were exhumed from a field a few km (miles) south of Vukovar, main town in the enclave of Eastern Slavonia captured by separatist minority Serbs in a 1991 revolt against Croatia's move to independence from Yugoslavia.
Investigators believe Serb militia killed some 200 patients from the Vukovar hospital after seizing the town.
The Hague tribunal has indicted three Yugoslav army officers for war crimes and crimes against humanity over the Ovcara killings but all remain at large.
The investigation will include establishing the nature of injuries and the cause of death, and then the identification of victims, Strinovic said.
After enough evidence is gathered for the needs of the ICTY Croatian experts would complete identification of the remaining bodies, he said.
The excavation of the Ovcara site began on August 30 and was completed on Friday. Eastern Slavonia is the last Serb-held enclave in Croatia, due to revert to government rule some time next year.
